paragraphs.title: God Dwells in the Temple and Fulfills His Promise

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Then said Solomon.”
easy.q: Who said that the LORD would dwell in the thick darkness?

easy.explanation: Solomon said, “I have built an house of habitation for thee.”
easy.q: What did Solomon build for the LORD?

easy.explanation: He said, “In it have I put the ark.”
easy.q: What did Solomon put in the house?

medium.explanation: The LORD chose Jerusalem for His name.
medium.q: Which city did the LORD choose for His name?

medium.explanation: David’s son was to build the house.
medium.q: Who was to build the house according to the LORD’s word to David?

medium.explanation: Solomon describes the Temple as a dwelling place for the LORD.
medium.q: What does “an house of habitation” describe in this passage?

challenge.explanation: The LORD performed His word, and Solomon built the house.
challenge.q: How was God’s word to David related to the building of the Temple?

answers: No city or ruler was chosen
challenge.explanation: The LORD chose Jerusalem and David over Israel.
challenge.q: What change in God’s choice is described after the exodus from Egypt?

answers: It was connected with the LORD’s covenant
It was a residence for the people
challenge.explanation: The ark contained the covenant of the LORD.
challenge.q: What does placing the ark in the house show about the Temple?

paragraphs.title: Solomon Begins His Prayer Before the People

easy.explanation: He stood in the presence of all the congregation of Israel.
easy.q: Before whom did Solomon stand?

easy.explanation: The passage says he spread forth his hands.
easy.q: What did Solomon spread forth?

easy.explanation: He stood upon the brazen scaffold in the court.
easy.q: Where did Solomon stand as he prayed?

medium.explanation: He stood before the altar of the LORD.
medium.q: What did Solomon do before speaking his prayer?

medium.explanation: The text says he kneeled down upon his knees.
medium.q: What position did Solomon take on the scaffold?

medium.explanation: It was a bronze platform placed in the court.
medium.q: What was the brazen scaffold?

answers: The people participated in the solemn assembly
The people had left the Temple
challenge.explanation: All the congregation stood during the occasion.
challenge.q: What does the congregation’s standing suggest?

answers: He stood on the scaffold and kneeled upon his knees
He sat on the throne and bowed
challenge.explanation: Both actions are described in the passage.
challenge.q: How did Solomon combine standing and kneeling?

challenge.explanation: He spread his hands toward heaven.
challenge.q: Toward what did Solomon spread his hands?

paragraphs.title: The Covenant and the Promise to David’s Dynasty

answers: The keeper of the covenant and mercy
easy.explanation: Solomon praises the LORD who keeps covenant and shows mercy.
easy.q: How does Solomon describe the LORD?

easy.explanation: The promise was spoken to David.
easy.q: To whom was the promise in Solomon’s prayer given?

easy.explanation: They must take heed to their way and walk in God’s law.
easy.q: What must David’s children do for the dynasty to continue?

answers: The LORD’s promise to David had been fulfilled
medium.explanation: The LORD had fulfilled what He promised David.
medium.q: What had already happened according to Solomon?

medium.explanation: The children must walk in God’s law.
medium.q: What condition is connected with the promise of the throne?

answers: The royal line would not come to an end
A man would not be built
medium.explanation: The promise concerns a continuing line on Israel’s throne.
medium.q: In context, what does “There shall not fail thee a man” mean?

answers: The promise is connected with obedience
challenge.explanation: The continuation of the dynasty is linked to walking in God’s law.
challenge.q: What connection does Solomon show between promise and responsibility?

answers: God spoke and fulfilled His word
challenge.explanation: God spoke with His mouth and fulfilled it with His hand.
challenge.q: How does Solomon describe God’s word and action?

answers: So the royal promise will stand
So a wall can be built
challenge.explanation: He asks that the promised dynasty remain established.
challenge.q: Why does Solomon ask God to verify His word to David?

paragraphs.title: The Temple Cannot Contain God but Is a Place of Connection

easy.explanation: Solomon says they cannot contain Him.
easy.q: Can heaven and the heaven of heavens contain God?

easy.explanation: He asks God to have respect to his prayer and supplication.
easy.q: What does Solomon ask God to regard?

easy.explanation: He says, “day and night.”
easy.q: When does Solomon ask God’s eyes to be open upon the house?

answers: A place where people pray toward God
medium.explanation: The house is a place toward which prayer is directed.
medium.q: If God cannot be contained, what is the Temple’s role?

medium.explanation: The prayer says, “when thou hearest, forgive.”
medium.q: What does Solomon ask God to do when He hears from heaven?

answers: God is greater than heaven and the Temple
medium.explanation: Even heaven cannot enclose or limit God.
medium.q: What does “cannot contain thee” mean in this passage?

answers: God cannot be contained by the house, yet people pray toward it
God is present only in the house
Prayer has no connection with God
challenge.explanation: Solomon rejects the idea that the Temple confines God while calling it a place of prayer.
challenge.q: What tension appears in Solomon’s words?

answers: To show that the Temple does not limit God
To deny the value of the Temple
challenge.explanation: God hears from His dwelling place in heaven.
challenge.q: Why does Solomon mention God hearing from heaven?

answers: The house is the chosen place toward which prayer is directed
The name belongs only to the king
challenge.explanation: The house is where God said He would put His name.
challenge.q: How are God’s name and prayer connected?

paragraphs.title: The Temple as a Place of Justice, Repentance, and Help in Trouble

easy.explanation: He asks God to judge His servants.
easy.q: What does Solomon ask God to do when one man sins against another?

easy.explanation: The people may be defeated because they sinned.
easy.q: What could cause Israel to be put to the worse before an enemy?

easy.explanation: He asks God to send rain upon the land.
easy.q: What does Solomon ask for after drought?

answers: Return, confess God’s name, and pray
medium.explanation: The people are to return, confess, pray, and make supplication.
medium.q: What should Israel do after being defeated by an enemy?

answers: Forgive and render according to his ways
medium.explanation: He asks God to forgive and render to every man according to his ways.
medium.q: What does Solomon ask God to do for the repentant person?

medium.explanation: Blasting is listed with mildew, locusts, and caterpillers as agricultural troubles.
medium.q: What is “blasting” in the list of troubles?

answers: Trouble, prayer, repentance, and God’s response
Trouble, exile, and closing the house
challenge.explanation: The passages repeatedly describe turning to God and asking forgiveness.
challenge.q: What pattern appears in the descriptions of trouble?

answers: God can judge each person rightly
challenge.explanation: God’s knowledge of the heart supports His just judgment.
challenge.q: Why does Solomon say that God alone knows the hearts of men?

answers: That the people may walk rightly
That the people may stop praying
That the people may leave the land
challenge.explanation: Solomon asks God to teach them the good way in which they should walk.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of teaching the good way?

paragraphs.title: The Temple Is Open to the Foreigner and to Those at War

easy.explanation: Solomon mentions the stranger who is not of Israel.
easy.q: Who besides Israel is included in Solomon’s prayer?

easy.explanation: The stranger may come from a far country.
easy.q: From where might the stranger come?

answers: The chosen city and the house
easy.explanation: They would pray toward the chosen city and the house.
easy.q: Toward what would Israel pray when going to war?

medium.explanation: The stranger comes for God’s great name, mighty hand, and stretched-out arm.
medium.q: Why does the stranger come to the Temple?

answers: Hear and do according to his request
medium.explanation: Solomon asks God to hear from heaven and do all that the stranger calls for.
medium.q: What does Solomon ask God to do when the stranger prays?

answers: That God hear their prayer and maintain their cause
That the army stay in the city
medium.explanation: He asks God to hear their prayer and maintain their cause.
medium.q: What does Solomon ask during Israel’s war?

answers: All people of the earth will know and fear God’s name
challenge.explanation: The purpose is that all people may know and fear God’s name.
challenge.q: What should result when God answers the stranger?

answers: It is open to a sincere seeker who is not an Israelite
It is only for the king
It is closed to every foreigner
challenge.explanation: Solomon explicitly includes the foreigner who prays there.
challenge.q: What does mentioning the stranger reveal about the Temple?

answers: Israel prays toward the chosen city and Temple while going to war
The house goes with the army
The city is abandoned before prayer
challenge.explanation: The soldiers pray toward the place chosen by God.
challenge.q: How are the city, the house, and warfare connected?

answers: They may leave the law without consequence
easy.explanation: He says, “If they sin against thee.”
easy.q: What possibility does Solomon acknowledge concerning Israel?

answers: To a far-off or near land
easy.explanation: The passage mentions a land far off or near.
easy.q: Where might captives be taken?

answers: That they be open and attentive to prayer
That they turn away from the house
easy.explanation: He asks for open eyes and attentive ears.
easy.q: What does Solomon ask concerning God’s eyes and ears?

answers: Think upon their ways, turn, and pray
medium.explanation: They are to bethink themselves, turn, and pray.
medium.q: What should Israel do while in captivity?

answers: With all their heart and soul
medium.explanation: The text says, “with all their heart and with all their soul.”
medium.q: How completely should they return to God?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the king who was anointed.
medium.q: What does “thine anointed” refer to at the end of the chapter?

answers: Sin, punishment and exile, repentance, and forgiveness
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from sin and captivity to confession, prayer, and forgiveness.
challenge.q: What sequence does Solomon describe concerning sin and exile?

answers: They direct prayer toward God’s chosen place
They want to move away from Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Even in captivity, they pray toward the places God chose.
challenge.q: Why do the captives pray toward their land, city, and house?

answers: It asks God to arise and dwell with the ark in the Temple
It cancels the building of the house
challenge.explanation: The conclusion asks God to arise into His resting place with the ark of His strength.
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with the beginning of the chapter?
